Promote cross-project learning and sharing of good practices through mentoring, peer support, training, and documentation of lessons learned. Contribute to country-office portfolio reviews, annual planning, and research-management discussions. Identify recurring implementation challenges and contribute to improvements in research SOPs, tools, templates, systems, and management practices. Share lessons and good practices across projects and contribute to a culture of research excellence, financial responsibility, compliance, and continuous improvement. Undertake other responsibilities assigned in support of IPA Uganda's research and organizational objectives. At least 4-5 years of relevant professional experience. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or workstreams simultaneously and deliver against competing deadlines. Working knowledge of quantitative research methods and experience implementing rigorous research designs; experience with randomized controlled trials is a strong plus. Experience supervising field research, including survey design and implementation, field teams, data collection, monitoring, and data-quality assurance. Working knowledge of at least one statistical software package such as Stata, R, or Python. Experience with electronic data-collection platforms such as SurveyCTO, KoboToolbox, ODK, or similar systems. Strong project-management skills, including work planning, risk management, problem-solving, documentation, and follow-through. Strong budgeting and financial-management skills, including the ability to read project financial reports, monitor expenditure and forecasts, and identify financial risks. Experience preparing donor or partner reports and contributing to grant proposals or funding applications. Strong interpersonal and stakeholder-management skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with researchers, partners, and colleagues from diverse backgrounds. Ability to work independently, manage ambiguity, and exercise sound judgment within delegated authority. Flexible and proactive work ethic and demonstrated alignment with IPA's mission and standards. Full professional fluency in written and spoken English. Willingness and ability to travel up to 30%. Experience working in Uganda or a comparable low- or middle-income country research environment (preferred). Familiarity with research ethics and regulatory processes, including IRB/REC and UNCST requirements (preferred). Experience managing donor-funded research projects or grants (preferred). Experience working directly with PIs, donors, or implementing partners (preferred). Location Based in Uganda. Ability and willingness to travel up to 30% for field oversight, project meetings, and stakeholder engagement, including travel to various project sites. IPA brings together researchers and decision-makers to design, rigorously evaluate, and refine these solutions and their applications, ensuring that the evidence created is used to improve the lives of people living in poverty. IPA exists to bring together leading researchers and these decision-makers to ensure that the evidence we create leads to a tangible impact on the world. Since its founding in 2002, IPA has worked with over 600 leading academics to conduct over 1,000 evaluations in 52 countries. This research has informed hundreds of successful programs that now impact millions of individuals worldwide. As IPA adheres to strict safeguarding principles, selected candidates will be expected to adhere to these standards. By joining IPA, you become part of a team dedicated to ethical conduct, social responsibility, and meaningful impact in the fight against global poverty. Together, we work to create a better world where everyone has the opportunity to thrive with dignity and respect.
